newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian G-Bank, Kredietbank renew poison pills.
newsitem.headline: Belgian G-Bank, Kredietbank renew poison pills.

text.p: Shareholders of Belgian banks Generale Bank and Kredietbank approved the renewal of anti-takeover poison pills at extraordinary shareholder meetings on Thursday.

Generale Bank shareholders approved the renewal of a capital authorisation worth seven billion francs for a five-year period, giving the board of directors the right to issue new capital for that amount without prior shareholder approval.
"The authorised capital can be used to prevent...a destabilisation of shareholdership, which could be the result of a potential or real hostile takeover bid," Generale Bank said in a statement.
Kredietbank shareholders approved the issue of 20 nominative call warrants, with the elimination of preference rights, in favour of Kredietbank leading shareholder Almanij.
Each warrant gives the right to subscribe to 100,000 new Kredietbank shares at a price which is the average of the bourse prices of the 30 days preceeding the exercise.

They can be exercised at any moment from June 1997 to June 2001 if there are indications that the controlling majority of Kredietbank shareholders is threathened or in case of a hostile bid for the bank.
